content.user_title: Build a Data Capability Enablement Plan
content.value_statement: Organizations often struggle to separate platform automation from work requiring human judgment. This skill creates coordinated platform and training plans for distinct roles.
actual_capabilities: Assesses which data asset activities should be automated or retained for human judgment.
Creates phased platform roadmaps covering diagnosis, module design, delivery planning, and final coordination.
Designs role-based training matrices for executives, finance, data teams, and business teams.
Defines deliverables, quality checks, assessment criteria, and reference pricing assumptions.
Coordinates platform planning and training design into one data capability enablement proposal.
limitations: Does not provide legal, accounting, valuation, or regulatory opinions.
Does not guarantee data recognition, financing, trading, or platform adoption outcomes.
Requires current organizational goals, systems, roles, and data literacy information.
Policy references and pricing assumptions require verification before external use.

use_cases.title: Plan an Enterprise Enablement Program
use_cases.description: Separate automation opportunities from human decisions, then create a phased platform and training roadmap.

use_cases.title: Design Role-Based Data Training
use_cases.description: Build differentiated course paths, exercises, and assessments for four organizational role groups.

use_cases.title: Consolidate Data Asset Tools
use_cases.description: Map existing tools into platform modules, identify gaps, and plan user training for deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Capability Priorities
prompt_templates.prompt: Our goal is [goal]. Our current systems are [systems]. Identify the first platform and training priorities for [roles].
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a concise capability assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Separate Automation and Judgment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these activities: [activities]. Classify each as automatable, human-led, or hybrid. Explain the boundary and required controls.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Role-Based Curriculum
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a curriculum for executives, finance, data teams, and business teams. Include objectives, source materials, duration, practice, and assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Integrated Delivery Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [goals], [tools], [roles], [constraints], and [timeline], create an integrated platform roadmap and training plan. Include deliverables, dependencies, quality checks, risks, and assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce an advanced end-to-end enablement plan.

output_examples.input: Assess whether our inventory, quality, ledger, and commercialization tools should become one platform.
output: Current-state module map with overlaps and gaps

output_examples.input: Create training for executives, finance, data specialists, and business teams.
output: Separate learning objectives for each role
Courses limited to practical session lengths

output_examples.input: Prepare a complete data capability enablement proposal.
output_examples.output: A phased proposal covering diagnosis, boundaries, platform modules, curriculum, deliverables, quality checks, risks, and assumptions.

best_practices: Provide clear goals, current tools, role groups, constraints, and data literacy levels.
Verify policies, prices, and timelines against current authoritative sources.
Remove sensitive client data from cases, examples, and public training materials.
anti_patterns: Do not use one identical curriculum for every organizational role.
Do not automate activities before defining where human judgment remains necessary.
Do not present training or platform deployment as a guaranteed compliance or financing result.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide your target outcome, current systems, available tools, role groups, timeline, constraints, and data literacy baseline.

faq.question: Can this skill design a complete platform?
faq.answer: It can propose modules, gaps, controls, and a roadmap. It does not implement or operate the platform.

faq.question: Which audiences can the training cover?
faq.answer: The framework supports executives, finance staff, data teams, business teams, and general industry audiences.

faq.question: Does it provide legal or accounting conclusions?
faq.answer: No. Qualified professionals must provide legal, accounting, valuation, and regulatory conclusions.

faq.question: Can it estimate delivery effort and price?
faq.answer: It can provide reference ranges and assumptions. Confirm final prices using scope, participants, duration, and customization needs.

faq.question: How does it protect sensitive data?
faq.answer: The guidance requires anonymized cases and excludes real client data from public training. Users must apply organizational security controls.
